items.title: AI Could Make Films Costlier Than the 35mm Era, Korean Pioneers Warn
items.excerpt: At TCCF in Taipei, Studio Meta-K CEO Kim Kwang-jib said the token bill alone for a 100-minute AI feature can top KRW500 million ($366,000) with top commercial tools, and that every revision is a paid re-render, so piecemeal client notes can multiply costs tenfold. He and MBC C&I's Lee Sang-wook, whose AI feature 'Raphael' heads to Korean cinemas, also covered hybrid shoots and new crew roles.

items.title: Two 'Ramayana' Cuts Are in Theaters — but Your Best Bet for the Indian Epic Is Clear
items.excerpt: The English cut of DNEG/Prime Focus's 'Ramayana' uses an in-house AI lip-sync tool called 'Brahma AI' that maps newly captured English mouth performances, recorded by real actors (sometimes the original cast), onto the original faces. IndieWire's critic says the visual dub makes the English performances stilted and recommends the Hindi version.

items.title: View Conference Was Inspiring: The AI Sales Pitches Were Exhausting (And Occasionally Bullshit)
items.excerpt: Cartoon Brew pushes back on the generative-AI pitches at Turin's View Conference: NVIDIA's Richard Kerris and Jeff Kember and Runway's Cristobal Valenzuela, including the session 'Every Pixel Will Be Generated'. It notes that directors Januel Mercado and McKenna Harris said they don't use gen AI, which undercuts the claim that everyone already does.
